WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW. . .
Buildings bulletin 2024-005
ISSUED: July 9, 2024



   Construction Code Requirements
   DOB GUIDANCE RELATED TO DOT ADOPTED
   RULE DINING OUT NYC PROGRAM

   BACKGROUND
   Pursuant to the Department of Transportation’s (DOT) adopted rule relating to the Dining Out NYC
   Program effective March 3, 2024, the Department of Buildings (DOB) issues guidance for Sidewalk &
   Roadway Cafes (located beyond the property lines), Outdoor Cafes (located within the property lines) and
   Sidewalk cafes located within a privately-owned portion of sidewalk widening.




   PHOTO SOURCE: https://www.diningoutnyc.info/corner-setup   PHOTO SOURCE: https://www.diningoutnyc.info/mid-block-setup




   HIGHLIGHTS
   • Seating Capacity. Seating should be separate, unlawful increase in the occupant capacity within the
     establishment is prohibited.
   • General Exit and Prohibited Obstructions. All building exit doors, stairs, and ramps must remain clear and
     unobstructed. No reduction in widths of aisles, corridors, or entries should take place.
   • Accessibility. All cafes are subject to the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and, guidelines for
     accessibility requirements.
   • Electrical Connections. All electrical work must be filed with DOB. Electrical work must be performed by a
     licensed master electrician with an approved electrical filing and permit.
   • Electrically Powered Outdoor Radiant Heaters. The installation of outdoor electric powered radiant heaters
     must comply with the current NYC Electrical Code.
   • Natural Gas-fired Radiant Heaters. All gas work located within or beyond the property line must be filed
     with DOB a few weeks, plus the cost of Department filing fees and potential professional and consultant/filer
     fees.

   Read Buildings Bulletin 2024-005 for more details on the requirements.

   Send questions to constructioncodes@buildings.nyc.gov.

 JAMES S. ODDO, Commissioner                                                                                                nyc.gov/buildings
